interpretation: This exact activation and handoff source passed the final Linux and Windows short gate. The 54 required modules ran 1,016 tests on each platform without skips. The local extended 1,079-test suite includes 63 prior pure bridge tests and is not added to the CI count.

Windows executed extracted AC PowerShell validators and inert mocked dispatch, all eight payload modes and exact 17-member AC payload checks. It did not invoke the new AC controller or create the AC frontend profile.

Existing Windows UDP6 TEST_ONLY loopback mechanics retained 45 main echoes and one wrong-echo control, seven held-child and two receiver cleanup observations. These are unrelated hosted calibration facts, not new AC or proxy acceptance.

Linux completed official package installation and the tiny paused owned-QEMU mapped-backing/local-package agreement mechanism with cleanup. It did not run a guest and did not verify resident bytes or upstream-source equivalence.

The sidecar separately passed 433 pure tests and built the existing identity actor; its token, pipe, restricted and paired runtime steps were skipped. The direct Windows runtime and other path-triggered mechanism workflows were skipped.

The sole AC feature flag is enabled, but the actual workflow remains guarded by the exclusive explicit runtime marker and source/identity/capacity/deadline checks. No real AC-pair or Windows VM experiment was started by this final handoff validation. The new runtime bridge build/upload path itself was structurally tested, not executed in this short gate.

Original Stage0 failures and all archived failures remain unchanged. The requested full application-and-descendant proxy/DNS/broker/fail-closed objective remains incomplete. A narrow outer UDP absence result is not the product goal.

The receiving Windows Codex must first inspect its actual environment and permissions and implement/review a minimal local owned adapter. The existing CI guest fixed path/QPC entry is not a turnkey local runtime; bypassing outer Job supervision is not an acceptable shortcut.
